researched_by: local press coverage of council decisions through 2024
policy_summary:
Parking is allowed in council car parks; sleeping overnight is prohibited. The four-site 'Pembs Stop' scheme approved in February 2024 was rejected at scrutiny in April after objections from Visit Pembrokeshire and local campsite operators, and cut to a single site by September.

UPDATED: a two-year trial launched in late April 2026, concentrating overnight parking at heavily monitored ferry-linked sites, principally Goodwick Moor. GBP10 a night, capped at ONE night - not the two nights in the original proposal.
notes: The clearest case of provision blocked by the campsite industry rather than by residents. Worth carrying into the hostility index: opposition comes from competitors as often as from communities. Note also the trial got smaller and stricter each time it was revised - four sites to one, two nights to one.
open_questions: Which sites beyond Goodwick Moor are in the two-year trial? Tenby and Fishguard are mentioned as target areas.
Was Western Way Pembroke Dock added after the three-month review?
What does 'heavily monitored' mean - ANPR, wardens, or booking?
Are the Manorbier and Newgale on-street restrictions still in force?
